subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Acidity in Coffee
description: A quick win: understand Acidity in Coffee.

hook.text: Acidity in coffee isn't about pH. It's the bright, lively sensation that makes great coffee taste vibrant.

buildup.text: Citric acid tastes lemony. Malic acid tastes apple-like. Phosphoric gives a sparkling, cola-like brightness.

discovery.text: High-altitude beans develop more organic acids because slow ripening concentrates these compounds.

twist.text: Dark roasting destroys most acids. That's why dark roasts taste flatter and less complex than light roasts.

climax.text: Acidity is the backbone of specialty coffee. Without it, coffee tastes dull—like music without treble.

punchline.text: Not sour. Bright. Acidity is coffee's sparkle.

quiz.question: Why do high-altitude beans have more acidity?
